spec/line-monitoring.md.text:
# Production Line Monitoring

## Temperature readings
Each furnace sensor sends a temperature reading with the sensor id and a measurement timestamp.
A reading whose measurement timestamp is older than the last stored reading of the same sensor is discarded.
A reading with the same sensor id and measurement timestamp as a stored reading is ignored.

## Overheat alarm
When a stored reading is above 850 °C, an overheat alarm is raised for that furnace.
An alarm stays active until a shift supervisor acknowledges it.

## Shift supervisor
Only a shift supervisor can acknowledge alarms.

invariants: readings are stored in measurement order per sensor

requirements.source_statement: Sensor readings are stored in measurement order; stale and duplicate readings are not stored.
Readings above 850 °C raise an overheat alarm that stays active until acknowledged.
Only a shift supervisor can acknowledge alarms.

claims.text: A reading older than the last stored reading of the same sensor is discarded.
A reading repeating a stored sensor id and measurement timestamp is ignored.
A stored reading above 850 °C raises an overheat alarm for the furnace.
An overheat alarm stays active until a shift supervisor acknowledges it.
An operator who is not a shift supervisor cannot acknowledge an alarm.

tests.title: Stale reading is discarded
tests.objective: Verify that a reading older than the last stored one is discarded.
tests.state: sensor with a stored reading at 10:00:05
tests.trigger: sensor sends a reading measured at 10:00:01
tests.expected: The older reading is discarded and the stored reading stays 10:00:05.
tests.priority_reason: Out-of-order data would corrupt the furnace history.

tests.title: Duplicate reading is ignored
tests.objective: Verify that a reading repeating a stored timestamp is ignored.
tests.state: sensor with a stored reading at 10:00:05
tests.trigger: sensor sends the same reading again
tests.expected: The duplicate reading is ignored and only one reading exists for 10:00:05.

tests.title: Reading above the limit raises an alarm
tests.objective: Verify that a stored reading above 850 °C raises an overheat alarm.
tests.expected: An overheat alarm is raised for the furnace.

tests.title: Alarm stays active until acknowledged
tests.objective: Verify that an overheat alarm remains active without acknowledgement.
tests.trigger: a later reading of 700 °C arrives without acknowledgement

tests.title: Operator cannot acknowledge an alarm
tests.objective: Verify that an operator without the supervisor role cannot acknowledge alarms.
tests.trigger: operator tries to acknowledge the alarm
tests.expected: The acknowledgement is refused and the alarm stays active.
tests.indivisible_contract: the refusal is observed as the alarm remaining active

questions.question: What must happen to readings buffered by the gateway while the network is down?
questions.reason: The specification does not describe buffering or replay.

dimensions.summary: Invalid readings were reviewed; the specification defines no validation beyond ordering and duplicates.

candidates.description: A reading of exactly 850 °C does not raise an alarm.

test.title: Reading at exactly the limit raises no alarm
test.objective: Verify that 850 °C, which is not above the limit, raises no alarm.
test.expected: No overheat alarm is raised for the furnace.

dimensions.summary: Human interactions are limited to alarm acknowledgement.

candidates.description: An operator acknowledges an alarm meant for the supervisor.

intent.state: overheat alarm active on the furnace
intent.trigger: the operator acknowledges the alarm in place of the supervisor
intent.expected: the acknowledgement is refused and the alarm remains active

candidates.description: The supervisor acknowledges the alarm of the wrong furnace.
candidates.reason: the specification does not describe multiple simultaneous alarms or furnace selection during acknowledgement

patterns_reviewed.reason: data enters through sensors, not people; the only human action is acknowledgement
alarm selection during acknowledgement is not described

dimensions.summary: No user-facing input other than acknowledgement exists.
Alarm lifecycle active and acknowledged was reviewed; persistence is covered by the acceptance test.
Ingestion has three outcomes (stored, discarded, ignored) already covered by acceptance tests.
Two sensors reporting at once do not share state per the specification.
Ordering races are the out-of-order delivery reviewed in INTEGRATION.
Duplicate delivery is covered by the duplicate acceptance test.

candidates.description: The gateway delivers the same reading twice.

intent.trigger: the sensor reading is sent again by the gateway
intent.expected: the duplicate reading is ignored and only one reading is kept

dimensions.summary: Gateway delivery order and connectivity were reviewed.

candidates.description: Readings arrive in reverse measurement order.

intent.state: sensor with a newer stored reading
intent.trigger: the sensor sends an older reading that arrives late
intent.expected: the older reading is discarded and the stored reading stays unchanged

candidates.description: Readings produced while the gateway network is down.

test.title: Readings produced during a network outage
test.objective: Explore how readings produced during an outage reach storage once the network returns.
test.state: gateway network interrupted for five minutes
test.trigger: network is restored after the outage
test.expected: Stored readings never go back in measurement time for the sensor.
test.priority_reason: Outage behavior is undefined but data loss matters.

dimensions.summary: Recovery after an outage depends on the undefined buffering policy explored in INTEGRATION.
Failure surfaces were compared with the described architecture.

surfaces_reviewed.reason: the specification describes only sensor ingestion and alarms, with no cache, queue workers, sessions or retry policy

dimensions.summary: Sensor authentication is not described by the selected sources.
Supervisor-only acknowledgement is covered by an acceptance test.
Reading order and duplicates are covered by acceptance tests.
Interaction between discarded readings and alarms was reviewed.

test.title: Discarded stale reading raises no alarm
test.objective: Verify that a discarded reading above the limit does not raise an alarm.
test.state: sensor with a stored reading at 10:00:05 and no active alarm
test.trigger: sensor sends a reading of 900 °C measured at 10:00:01

dimensions.summary: No use case is documented; the reading-to-alarm journey is covered by composing ingestion and alarm tests.

test.title: Overheat reading to active alarm
test.objective: Verify the journey from an overheat reading to a persistent alarm.
test.expected: The overheat alarm stays active after the later reading.
